title: Nonlinear quantum noise polarization in macroscopic nonlinear QED
authors: Arman Kashef, Stefan Scheel, Marco Ornigotti
abstract: We construct a quantum theory of light in nonlinearly responding materials with dispersion   and absorption and, in particular, show the emergence of non-Gaussian noise associated with   nonlinear absorption processes. Our theory is based on a path-integral formulation of the   microscopic Huttner-Barnett model including cubic matter self-interaction required for   $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinear processes. We show that the noise polarization emerges naturally from   a decoupling of the stochastic weights of the bath response which, in case of cubic   self-interactions, leads to a decoupling via Airy functions. As the theory is, by   construction, consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, it constitutes   a viable quantum theory of light in nonlinear media.
summary: This paper develops a quantum theory for light in nonlinear, absorbing materials by extending the Huttner-Barnett model to include cubic self-interactions. Using the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral, the authors derive that the nonlinear response necessitates the emergence of non-Gaussian noise polarization. This provides a quantum-statistically consistent framework for nonlinear macroscopic QED.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct a quantum theory of light propagating in nonlinear, absorbing media that remains consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem.
main_result: The theory successfully incorporates non-Gaussian noise polarization arising from cubic self-interactions, providing a quantum-statistically consistent framework for nonlinear macroscopic QED.
method: The analysis heavily relies on the Schwinger-Keldysh path-integral formalism, employing auxiliary field transformations (using Airy functions) to decouple the cubic interaction term.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum theory of light in a nonlinear medium, modeled by extending the Huttner-Barnett framework to include a cubic matter self-interaction ($\chi^{(3)}$).
key_observables: Noise polarization field, non-Gaussian noise spectrum, linear and nonlinear susceptibilities ($\chi^{(1)}, \chi^{(2)}$), and the noise correlation function $\langle P^{(1)}_{\xi}(\omega)P^{(1)}_{\xi}(\omega')angle$.
important_parameters: The nonlinear coupling constant ($\lambda$), the bath spectral density, and the frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The theory is assumed to be consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and the derivation involves treating the cubic term via an auxiliary field transformation using Airy functions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the interaction vertices for the $\chi^{(3)}$ theory, showing terms like $V_{ccq}$ and $V_{qqq}$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the necessity of the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, to applying the Keldysh formalism, and finally using an auxiliary field transformation based on Airy functions to decouple the cubic action and derive the noise statistics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it provides a rigorous, non-perturbative method for handling nonlinear dissipation and noise sources in quantum light-matter interactions.
